main_text.p: tisthenem, Zenonem, Empedoclem, Epicharmum, Hippasum, Philolaum, Heraclitum, Xenophanem, Parmenidem, Melissum, Leucippum, Democritum, Diogenem, Mnesiorem: Paucis dicam: Fecere peregrinationum studia, ut in Naturæ studio excolendo palmam omnibus fere Graeci præripuerint.

E Graecia tandem in Italiam, & inde in Germaniam nostram Musæ migrarunt: in quâ, præter divina & alia humanitatis studia, Naturæ quoque floret Contemplatio, sedem melioribus hisce studijs Germaniæ Principibus intra sua territoria vbique figentibus, docentesque pariter & discentes ad honesta certamina liberalitate sua provocantibus. Quos inter & sua profitentur nomina Illustrissimi Principes Anhaltini, Dominimei clementissimi, quibus otium Musæ meæ, & Physicas hasce contemplationes, quibus scribo, studiosi Naturæ juvenes debent.

Originem & progressum Physiologiæ hactenus delineavi: præstantiam ac divinitatem ejus in exordio laudavi: quam tamen omnibus nondum persuasam opinor. Physicas [?] vetustiores [?]Nam & ante Platonem, testis Plutarchus, me-teorolesschas [?]teorolesschas Physicos profanum vulgus appellavit, quod meras de sublimium ratione nugas

page.notes: Left margin notes are partly unclear: the first line reads "Physicas" followed by a word I could not read ("osons" or similar), and the second is a Greek-looking word rendered in Latin letters, "teorolesschas". Both are marked [?]. The word "Dominimei" is set as printed, with a possible word break after "Domini". The ornament before "Musæ meæ" and the mark beside "Anhaltini" are not transcribed. The right-hand strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is left out. The top line of the page is a fragment, so it is marked cont="true". No page number, catchword or signature is printed.
